A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and complete 24-page documents, including Appendices A–C. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the methods, equations, proofs, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original semi-synthetic decoding experiments in Section 4 and MMLU/MT-Bench evaluations, sensitivity analyses, and examples in Section 5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 5.1 retain the same sliding reflection window, entropy-based pausing criterion, and fixed-length beam-search refinement procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MMLU subjects and MT-Bench tasks, including the sanity-check scenarios and the social-science and college-subject analyses in Appendix B.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: greedy decoding and beam search in Tables 1, 6–7, and 11, and Top-k/Top-p sampling in Tables 2 and 12–15.

E3.justification: The model configurations, beam size of 4, default window size of 4, entropy threshold of 0.5, sampling settings, MMLU accuracy metric, and GPT-4o MT-Bench judging procedure are unchanged.

E4.justification: The window-size and entropy-threshold sensitivity studies, regeneration-ratio analyses, and three MT-Bench examples are identical in Section 5.4 and Appendix B. Correcting a table reference adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No statistical or uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains Phi3-Medium macro accuracies of 78.14% for greedy decoding, 76.44% for beam search, and 78.15% for reflection-window decoding; appendix results also match.

T1.justification: Definitions 3.1–3.2, Assumptions 3.3–3.5, Theorem 3.6, and the full proof in Appendix A are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about autoregressive decoding's suboptimality, selective refinement, and performance and efficiency relative to existing decoding approaches.

C2.justification: The necessary-but-not-sufficient qualification around Theorem 3.6, beam-search approximation discussion, and interpretations of performance, efficiency, and hyperparameter sensitivity remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, model identifiers, hyperparameters, and evaluation instructions are unchanged. No implementation, hardware, training-time, or code/data access information is added.

R1.justification: The cited works and research-positioning passages are identical. Bibliography entries move across pages 9–11 because of the new acknowledgment; none is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 revises author affiliations, adds a funding acknowledgment on page 9, and corrects 'Table ??' to 'Table 9' in Appendix B.2. The scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Affiliation edits slightly alter first-page spacing, and the acknowledgment causes bibliography reflow across pages 9–11. All figures and tables retain their content, structure, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes the broken table reference in Appendix B.2 and explicitly discloses funding support through the new acknowledgment. These provide small improvements in navigation and transparency; the methods, proofs, experiments, and supporting evidence remain unchanged.
